CWE-89.title: SQL Injection
CWE-89.business_impact: An attacker can read, modify, or delete arbitrary data in the backing database, potentially exposing sensitive customer or financial records and undermining data integrity.
CWE-89.remediation: Use parameterized queries or an ORM with bound parameters for all database access; never concatenate untrusted input into SQL strings. Apply least-privilege database accounts and validate/allowlist input where feasible.

CWE-79.title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
CWE-79.business_impact: An attacker can execute arbitrary script in a victim's browser session, enabling session hijacking, credential theft, or defacement of the application.
CWE-79.remediation: Contextually encode/escape all untrusted output rendered in HTML, JS, or URL contexts. Apply a strict Content-Security-Policy and use templating engines with automatic output escaping enabled.

CWE-22.title: Path Traversal
CWE-22.business_impact: An attacker can read or write files outside the intended directory, potentially exposing configuration secrets or achieving remote code execution.
CWE-22.remediation: Resolve and canonicalize user-supplied paths, then verify they remain within an allowlisted base directory before use. Avoid passing raw user input directly to filesystem APIs.

CWE-287.title: Improper Authentication
CWE-287.business_impact: An attacker can bypass identity verification entirely, gaining unauthorized access to protected functionality or data.
CWE-287.remediation: Enforce authentication on every protected endpoint via centralized middleware/guards rather than ad-hoc per-route checks. Use well-vetted authentication libraries and require strong credential/session validation.

CWE-200.title: Exposure of Sensitive Information
CWE-200.business_impact: Sensitive internal data (configuration, credentials, PII) is disclosed to unauthorized parties, risking compliance violations and further compromise.
CWE-200.remediation: Apply strict output filtering and access controls on any endpoint or error message that could reveal internal state. Review logs, debug endpoints, and error traces for inadvertent data leakage.

CWE-538.title: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Externally-Accessible File or Directory
CWE-538.business_impact: Sensitive files (e.g. VCS metadata, environment configuration) are reachable by unauthenticated clients, potentially exposing credentials or source code.
CWE-538.remediation: Exclude sensitive directories (.git, .env, backups) from the web root or explicitly deny access to them at the reverse proxy/server configuration level.

CWE-502.title: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
CWE-502.business_impact: An attacker can craft malicious serialized payloads to achieve remote code execution or denial of service when deserialized by the application.
CWE-502.remediation: Avoid deserializing untrusted data with formats that support arbitrary object instantiation (e.g. pickle). Prefer safe data formats (JSON) with strict schema validation.

UNKNOWN.title: Unclassified Vulnerability
UNKNOWN.business_impact: This finding could not be matched to a known CWE category. Its business impact should be assessed manually based on the specific vulnerability details before this report is finalized.
UNKNOWN.remediation: Review the finding's evidence and CVSS vector manually, consult the relevant CWE taxonomy entry if one becomes available, and apply remediation guidance specific to the underlying weakness class.
